Use commas, parentheses, periods, or colons unless an em dash is clearly needed.
Avoid repeated forms such as “not X, but Y” and “not this, not that, just Z.”
Avoid strings such as “fast, safe, and scalable” unless the three items are necessary.
Avoid “The result? …”, “The problem? …”, and “Why? Because …”.
Remove phrases such as “something shifted,” “everything changed,” and “let that sink in.”
Do not make every paragraph the same length or use a repeated claim-explanation-summary pattern.
Use fewer headings, fewer bold phrases, fewer colon-heavy labels, and fewer bullet lists.
Avoid checkmarks, sparkles, arrows, fire icons, and decorative Unicode bullets.
Do not reflexively present both sides when the evidence supports a direct claim.
Do not restate the same idea at the end of every section.
End with a concrete implication, decision, test, or next action.
